CascadeGuard AI: Multi-Surface Engineering Blueprint

Autonomous Lateral Social Engineering & Account Takeover (ATO) Interceptor built "At the Glass" across WhatsApp Web, Telegram, and Android.

📌 1. Strategic Context: Why "Mitigation 4" (Multi-Surface)?

When attackers compromise accounts via QR phishing, SIM swapping, or rogue web sessions, they weaponize established trust. Traditional antivirus is blind because messages originate from authentic phone numbers; messaging platforms are blind because End-to-End Encryption (E2EE) prevents server inspection.

To eliminate platform ToS ban risks and provide defense across all user contexts, CascadeGuard implements a Multi-Surface Strategy:

SURFACE 1 WhatsApp Web (DOM)

Mechanism: Chromium Extension (Manifest v3) using a passive MutationObserver on stable accessibility nodes ([role="row"]).
ToS Defense: Zero clicks, zero WebSocket hooks. In-line shield injected into an isolated Shadow DOM overlay. Works like Grammarly.

SURFACE 2 Telegram Ecosystem

Mechanism: Official Open-Source TDLib / MTProto Client Plugin and Telegram Bot Security Gateway.
ToS Defense: Telegram's client is 100% open-source and officially supports custom clients without scraping or policy bans.

SURFACE 3 Android OS Companion

Mechanism: Android NotificationListenerService & AccessibilityService.
ToS Defense: Operates at the OS notification/intent layer (standard Truecaller / Google Play Protect security model). Zero app modification.

⚙️ 2. Multi-Agent Engine Architecture

The core engine performs a parallel dual-engine audit in < 300 milliseconds entirely on-device:

Agent 1: Stylometric Profiler
  • Cosine distance against local non-reversible user baseline
  • Hinglish vernacular ratio & colloquial slang tracking
  • Punctuation entropy (exclamations, comma shifts)
  • Casing pressure velocity (all-caps urgency bursts)
Agent 2: Forensic & Intent Scanner
  • Financial coercion & pressure keywords heuristics
  • UPI VPA regex extractor & QR payload parsing
  • Simulated I4C / NPCI Mule Account Registry query
  • Malicious APK & phishing contest links scanner
Agent 3: Autonomous Challenger & Interlock
  • Deploys in-line warning banner in Shadow DOM
  • Locks target UPI links & renders buttons unclickable
  • Generates Zero-Knowledge "Friend Quiz" verification challenge
Agent 4: Blast-Radius Containment
  • Maps real-time viral propagation attack topology
  • Flags compromised accounts in college & batch groups
  • Issues containment signal to group admins (zero chat text)

🎤 8. The Winning 3-Minute Hackathon Pitch Script

Minute 1: The Hook & The Problem (Weaponized Trust)

In India, account hijacking isn't about data theft—it is about weaponizing established interpersonal trust to execute cascading scams. Traditional antivirus is blind because messages come from authentic phone numbers, and WhatsApp servers cannot inspect chats due to End-to-End Encryption."

Minute 2: The Live Demonstration (300ms Interception)

"Watch what happens when an attacker sends a medical scam from our friend Rohit's compromised account. In under 300 milliseconds, CascadeGuard's on-device engine detects a 91% stylometric drift, extracts the suspicious UPI VPA, engages our Payment Interlock to disable direct payment, and generates a zero-knowledge 'Friend Quiz' verification challenge. Across the college hostel network, the attack is instantly quarantined before money is lost."

Minute 3: Privacy, Bharat Scale & The Moat

"Best of all, zero chat text ever leaves the user's device. Our Multi-Surface Architecture protects users on WhatsApp Web, Telegram, and Android OS without violating platform terms of service. By storing non-reversible mathematical fingerprints and enforcing zero network egress, CascadeGuard is 100% compliant with India's DPDP Act 2023. We are building the immune system for Bharat's digital communication."

🎯 9. Tough Judge Q&A Defense Playbook

Q: "Won't WhatsApp ban users for injecting into their web application?"
Answer: Meta bans tools that automate messaging, scrape contacts, or hook internal WebSockets. CascadeGuard operates strictly at the presentation layer—the exact same way Grammarly, 1Password, or screen-reader accessibility tools do. We use a read-only MutationObserver on stable accessibility nodes and render our shield inside an isolated Shadow DOM without touching WhatsApp's React tree.
Q: "Isn't a browser extension with chat access a massive spyware risk?"
Answer: Under Manifest v3, our Content Security Policy strictly enforces connect-src 'none'. It is cryptographically impossible for the extension to transmit messages to external servers. All text processing occurs in volatile RAM and is immediately discarded. Zero bytes of chat text leave the device.
Q: "What happens if a friend actually has a genuine emergency?"
Answer: CascadeGuard never blocks communications or deletes messages. It simply engages a payment interlock and offers a private relational challenge ("What was our hostel warden's nickname?"). A real friend answers in seconds, instantly unlocking the payment channel.
